findings.where: Where we're starting: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), each with its 'Best hostels ›' line, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards look clickable but do nothing. Each has a teal 'Best hostels' line in the link colour with a chevron, a raised shadow and a hover style, yet none of them is a link (parts p8 to p10). Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of the page's three jobs, and the hero's 'Explore destinations' button lands on these dead cards.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps 'Explore destinations' and then taps Canggu finds nothing happens and nowhere else to go. The page cannot send anyone to a guide.

findings.where: Nav bar 'How we rank'; footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank', 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every one of these links points back to this same page, so they act like links but lead nowhere. 'How we rank' sits in the main nav and is the only route to the merit-ranking claim the hero makes.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who doubts the 'ranks on merit alone' promise clicks 'How we rank' and just reloads the homepage. A visitor checking Privacy before sending their email gets nothing. On a site that hasn't launched yet, both make it look unfinished or untrustworthy.

findings.where: Where we're starting: the section heading
findings.fault: The section heading is set at about twice the size of the hero's MantaHostels h1 and fills the whole first view on desktop. It is the loudest thing on the page, louder than the brand line and the coral button, and it pushes the cards below the fold.
findings.who_objects: A visitor squinting at the page reads a section label as the main message and has to scroll past a wall of type to reach the destinations. The brand asks for loud moments with a calm area to work in, and this puts the loudest moment on a label in the sand area.

findings.where: Destination cards: the city names and the BALI / LOMBOK eyebrows
findings.fault: The city names and eyebrows are set in a monospace typewriter face. That face appears nowhere else on the page and isn't one of the brand faces (Quicksand for headings, Nunito Sans for labels). The cards look like code or a placeholder, not part of the site.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand sheet fixes the type, and a visitor, who sees the cards as clashing with the friendly beachy hero and reads them as unfinished.

findings.fault: The cards have a thick purple border. Purple isn't in the palette at all and has no job; cards should take a thin sand-coloured border.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because every colour has one job and card edges are meant to be sand. A visitor sees a loud colour that doesn't belong to the turquoise and sand brand.

findings.where: Destination cards: the shadow at rest
findings.fault: The cards sit under a wide, soft shadow at rest, stacked on top of a heavy border. The rules keep shadows for hover and popovers, and this shadow sells a lift and a clickability the cards don't have.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the rules say nothing sits at rest under a heavy shadow, and a visitor, who is promised a tap that does nothing.

findings.where: Hero: the eyebrow line, the MantaHostels h1 and the body paragraph
findings.fault: The biggest type in the hero is just the brand name, which the nav already shows. The vague claim 'The better way to find hostels' sits in a small eyebrow above it. The only text that says what the product does (merit-only ranking, then book with the hostel or your usual site) is the smallest, lightest text in the hero.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker giving the page five seconds sees a name and 'better way' but has to read fine print to learn why this is different. The brand asks for a loud claim with plain, specific mechanics beneath it, and here the loud line is the name, not a claim.

findings.where: Hero: the coral 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news' button, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The launch-news action is a mailto link with a sentence for a label, which wraps onto two ragged lines inside the pill on phone. Nothing says what the visitor will get or how often (one email at launch, no spam), and nothing says when the launch is.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone gets thrown into a mail app to write an email from scratch, with no idea what they're signing up for. Many won't bother, and that costs the page its main conversion.

findings.where: Hero buttons: the coral pill CTA and the square-cornered outline 'Explore destinations'
findings.fault: The two buttons have different corners: a full pill and a sharp square, while the system gives buttons 8px corners. Side by side they look like they come from two different sites.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the rules fix one control radius, and a visitor, who sees an unpolished pair of buttons right at the point of action.

findings.where: Nav bar, desktop: 'Destinations' against 'How we rank'
findings.fault: Only 'How we rank' is underlined, so two like nav links are treated differently. The underline hints it's special or the current page when it isn't, and the rules mark the current page with semibold, not an underline.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reads the odd underline as 'you are here' or as the only real link, so the nav gives them a wrong cue.

findings.where: Hero text column against the nav logo, the section heading and the cards, desktop
findings.fault: The hero copy and buttons start about 230px further right than the left edge shared by the nav logo, the section heading and the cards. The page has two left edges and no clear reason for it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning down the page loses the line their eye follows, so the hero looks off to one side.
